questions.question: Which actinide, discovered by Glenn T Seaborg in 1940, is used as a heat source for sensitive electrical components in satellites as well as a power source for satellites?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plutonium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plutonium **was discovered by **Glenn T Seaborg** in **1940.**
 
• It is a **silvery-gray actinide** metal that oxidizes to a **dull covering and tarnishes** when exposed to air.
 
• The element typically manifests in **four oxidation states **and **six allotropes.** 
 
• **Plutonium-238** is used as a** heat source** for sensitive electrical components in **satellites** as well as a power source for satellites.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Curium** is a **radioactive metallic element** and is used in the production of alpha particles for** cancer treatment.**

 
 
• It is also used in** heart pacemakers.**
 
 
 
• **Nobelium **is a synthetic element and has **no known uses.**
 
 
• Because of its radioactivity, it is** toxic**. 
 
 
 
• **Americium** is a radioactive element and is used in **smoke detectors** and as a source of **gamma radiation** for **industrial radiography.**
 
 
• The most prevalent form of Americium is** Americium-241.**

questions.question: The Jagannath Temple in Puri depicts which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form that originated in the state of** Odisha** in eastern India.
 
• The **Jagannath Temple in Puri **is one of the most famous **pilgrimage sites for Hindus** and is dedicated to **Lord Jagannath, **an incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
 
• The temple is known for its annual **Rath Yatra festival.**
 
• Odissi dance is an** integral part** of the rituals and traditions of the Jagannath Temple.
 
• The temple has a dedicated dance hall called the **Natamandira,** where Odissi performances are held during festivals and other special occasions.
 
• Odissi is characterized by its** graceful movements, intricate footwork, and expressive gestures**.
 
• It is known for its emphasis on the** tribhangi posture**, where the body is bent in three places - the head, torso, and knees.
 
• Odissi has a rich history and has evolved over the centuries, incorporating **elements** from other dance forms and cultural traditions.
 
• It is recognized as **one of the eight classical dance** forms of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Andhra Pradesh.**

 
 
• It is known for its fast-paced footwork and **dramatic storytelling.**
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
 
• It is known for its intricate **hand gestures and facial expressions.**
 
 
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form that originated in **northern India.**
 
 
• It is known for its fast footwork and **complex rhythmic patterns.**
 
 
 
• While these dance forms are not directly associated with the Jagannath Temple in Puri, they are important part of India's** rich cultural heritage** and have their own unique styles and traditions.

questions.question: A natural process of mechanical disintegration and or chemical decomposition of the rocks of the crust of the Earth by certain physical and chemical agencies of the atmosphere is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**weathering.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Weathering** is the natural process of **mechanical disintegration** and/or **chemical decomposition** of rocks due to **physical and chemical agents **of the atmosphere.
 
• Weathering can be caused by various factors such as **temperature changes, water, wind, and living organisms.**
 
• Weathering can lead to the **formation of soil, sedimentary rocks**, and **mineral deposits**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solidification of rocks:**

 
 
• This refers to the process of **molten rocks cooling and hardening** to form solid rocks.
 
• This process is also known as **crystallization**.
 
• **Igneous rocks** are formed through solidification.
 
 
 
• **New rock formation:**
 
 
• This can occur through various processes such as** volcanic activity,** where molten rocks are ejected from the** Earth's interior and solidify** on the surface.
 
• **Sedimentary rocks** can also form from the accumulation of sediment on the Earth's surface.

questions.question: In T20 cricket matches, a bowler can bowl a maximum of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 overs.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The maximum limit of overs per bowler has been set at **4 overs **to maintain the balance between the bat and ball and to ensure that the game remains **exciting and unpredictable**.
 
• If a bowler **exceeds his limit **of 4 overs, then it is considered as an** illegal delivery,** and the batting team is awarded a **run penalty.**
 
• In addition to **T20 cricket matches**, this rule also applies to other limited-overs cricket formats, such as **ODI **(One Day International) matches. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Each team in a Twenty20 match gets** one innings**, which can only be as long as **twenty overs.**
 
• An average Twenty20 match lasts roughly **two and a half hours,** with each innings lasting roughly **seventy minutes.**
 
• The official interval between innings is** ten minutes**.

questions.question: Name the longest highway single-tube tunnel that reduces the travel time and overall distance between Manali and Keylong.

• It reduces the travel distance between **Manali and Keylong **by **46 km** and the** travel time **by around **4-5 hours.**
 
• The tunnel is named after former Indian Prime Minister **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, who initiated the project in** 2002.**
 
• The construction of the tunnel was a challenging task due to the tough terrain and adverse weather conditions, but it was completed in a record time of **10 years.**
 
• The tunnel is a significant infrastructure development that not only provides a **better connectivity** but also boosts the economy of the region by promoting** tourism and trade.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natuwadi Tunnel** is a proposed tunnel.

 
 
• It will connect the **Natuwadi ghat of Maharashtra** with the **Konkan coast.**
 
 
 
• **Karbude Tunnel** is a railway tunnel.
 
 
• It is located in the **Ratnagiri** **district of Maharashtra**, India.
 
 
 
• **Jawahar Tunnel** is a road tunnel located in the** Pir Panjal range of Jammu and Kashmir,** India.
 
 
• It connects **Srinagar with Jammu.**

questions.question: Which institution launched the Self-Help Group - Bank Linkage Programme in 1992-93?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **SIDBI** (Small Industries Development Bank of India) is a **government-owned financial institution** that was set up in** 1990** to promote and finance **small-scale industries** in the country.
 
 
• It provides various services and schemes for the development of **micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs)** in India.

questions.question: The Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kutch and Sundarbans region provide ideal conditions for utilising _______ energy in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tidal.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tidal energy** is the correct answer for utilising in the **Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kutch **and **Sundarbans region** in India.
 
• Tidal energy is generated by the **gravitational forces** of the **moon and the sun** on the earth's water bodies.
 
• The Gulf of Khambhat and the Gulf of Kutch are known for their **strong tidal currents,** making them ideal locations for **tidal energy projects.**
 
• The Sundarbans region, located in the delta of the **Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna** rivers, has a vast network of **tidal creeks and channels **which can be used to generate tidal energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The most advanced and developed** renewable energy **source is **wind energy.**

 
 
• By harnessing the **kinetic energy** created by **air currents,** it uses wind to create electricity. 
 
 
 
• The energy present in a system that determines its** temperature** is referred to as** thermal energy**.
 
 
• Thermal energy flows as** heat.**
 
 
 
• Any energy produced by the sun is referred to as **solar energy.**
 
 
• **Nuclear fusion** occurs in the sun and produces solar energy.

questions.question: The Lomas Rishi cave which is a manmade cave is located in which state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Bihar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lomas Rishi cave** is a famous** man-made cave** located in the state of **Bihar, India.**
 
• The cave was built during the **Mauryan period,** between the** 3rd and 4th century **BCE, and is one of the earliest examples of **rock-cut architecture** in India.
 
• The Lomas Rishi cave is carved out of a** single granite rock** and is adorned with** intricate carvings and sculptures** of various deities, including **Lord Shiva, Lord Vishnu, and Goddess Durga.**
 
• The cave is also known for its unique architecture, featuring a **horseshoe-shaped entrance**, a **pillared veranda**, and a **square sanctum** with a **rock-cut lingam.**
 
• Apart from the Lomas Rishi cave, Bihar is also home to several other ancient rock-cut caves, such as the **Barabar Caves, the Nagarjuni Caves, and the Gopi Bigaha Caves.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharashtra** is a state in western India and is known for its rich cultural heritage, including ancient rock-cut caves such as the **Ajanta and Ellora caves.**
 
• **Karnataka** is a state in southern India and is known for its historic monuments and temples, such as the **Hampi ruins and the Chennakesava Temple.**
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is a state in central India and is known for its ancient rock-cut caves such as the **Bhimbetka caves and the Udayagiri Caves.**
 
• **Bihar** is a state in eastern India and is known for its rich history and cultural heritage, including ancient Buddhist and Hindu sites such as **Nalanda, Bodh Gaya, and Rajgir.**

questions.question: Commercialisation of agriculture is an indication of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marketable surplus.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Commercialisation of agriculture** refers to the process of **transforming agriculture **from a subsistence-based activity to a commercial enterprise.
 
• This involves producing **crops and goods **not only for personal consumption but also for **sale in the market.**
 
• When agriculture is commercialised, there is an increase in **marketable surplus, **which is the amount of agricultural produce that is available for sale in the market after meeting the **needs of the producers** and their families.
 
• This surplus can be sold for a** profit,** leading to an **increase in income** for the farmers.
 
• **Producers' surplus** refers to the** difference **between the price at which the producer is willing to sell a product and the **actual price** they receive in the market.
 
 
• This surplus is** maximised **when the producer is able to sell their product at a** higher price** than their cost of production.
 
 
 
• **Consumer surplus** refers to the difference between the price that **consumers are willing to pay** for a product and the actual price they pay.
 
 
• This surplus is maximised when the price of the product is **lower **than the value that consumers place on it.
 
 
 
• **Income surplus** refers to the **increase in income** that is generated as a result of commercialisation of agriculture.
 
 
• This surplus is maximised when the marketable surplus is sold at a price that is** higher than the cost of production.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term 'commercialisation of agriculture' is often associated with the **Green Revolution**, which was a period of significant agricultural innovation and productivity growth that occurred in the **1960s and 1970s.**
 
• The Green Revolution involved the introduction of **new crop varieties, improved irrigation systems**, and the **use of fertilisers and pesticides.**
 
• These innovations led to a significant increase in **agricultural productivity** and helped to** alleviate food shortages **in many parts of the world.
 
• However, there are also concerns about the **negative environmental **and **social impacts **of commercialisation of agriculture, such as **soil degradation, water pollution,** and displacement of** small-scale farmers.**
 
• In addition to marketable surplus, commercialisation of agriculture can also lead to the** emergence of agribusinesses**, which are large-scale, commercial enterprises that are involved in various aspects of agriculture, such as** production, processing, and distribution.**

questions.question: The first day of the Tamil calendar on 14 April is celebrated as ________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Puthandu **is also known as T**amil New Year's Day **and is celebrated on the first day of the** Tamil month of Chithirai. **
 
• The festival is observed by Tamils all over the world and is a time for **family gatherings, feasting, and exchanging gifts.**
 
• It is thought that **Lord Indra **arrived to earth on this auspicious day to bring about **harmony and tranquility**.
 
• It's also thought that **Lord Brahma **started the universe's creation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahamaham** is a festival celebrated in **Tamil Nadu** once every **12 years **at the** Mahamaham tank** in **Kumbakonam**.

 
 
• It is believed that taking a **dip in the tank d**uring the festival will wash away all sins and lead to salvation.
 
 
 
• **Onam** is a** harvest festival **celebrated in** Kerala** in honor of **King Mahabali**.
 
 
• It is a **ten-day festival **that falls in the Malayalam month of **Chingam** and is marked by feasting, boat races, and cultural programs.
 
 
 
• **Pongal** is a harvest festival celebrated in **Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana**.
 
 
• It is a** four-day** festival that falls in the Tamil month of **Thai** and is marked by the cooking of **sweet rice dishes** and the drawing of **Kolams** (rangoli) on the floor.

questions.question: Identify an endoparasite found in animals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flatworms.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **endoparasite** is a parasite that **lives inside the body** of its host.
 
• It may reside in the **digestive tract, blood vessels**, or other organs of the host animal.
 
• **Flatworms** are a type of endoparasite that can be found in a variety of** animals, including humans.**
 
• They are also known as** tapeworms or flukes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana** are both **marine animals** that belong to the **phylum Ctenophora**, also known as **comb jellies.**

 
 
• They are **carnivorous** and feed on **small planktonic animals.**
 
 
 
• **Adamsia** is a type of **sea anemone **that lives in symbiosis with certain species of **hermit crabs**.
 
 
• The crab provides protection for the** anemone,** while the anemone provides a source of **food for the crab.**

questions.question: The compound in which a hydroxy group, -OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has two other carbon atoms attached to it is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**secondary alcohol.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **hydroxy group (-OH) **attached to a saturated carbon atom with **two other carbon atoms** attached to it is known as a **secondary alcohol.**
 
• There are two alkyl groups present; their structures can **differ or be the same.**
 
• Secondary alcohol examples include **2 – propanol and 2 – butanol.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary alcohols** have the hydroxy group attached to a carbon atom with **only one other carbon atom **attached to it.
 
• In the case of a **tertiary alcohol**, the hydroxy group is attached to a saturated carbon atom with **three other carbon atoms** attached to it.
 
• An **aldehyde** is a compound that contains a** carbonyl group** (-C=O) attached to at least **one hydrogen atom.**
 
 
• This group is always located at the **end of a carbon chain.**

questions.question: Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibushan awardee, Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, was instrumental in reviving which of the following classical dances?
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Odissi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibushan** awardee,** Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra**, was instrumental in reviving the classical dance form of **Odissi.**
 
• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was a renowned Indian** classical dancer and choreographer **who played a significant role in popularizing Odissi dance form across the world.
 
• Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India that originated in the eastern state of** Odisha**.
 
• It has a rich history and is known for its **graceful movements, expressions, and intricate footwork.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Andhra Pradesh**.

 
 
• It is known for its fast-paced footwork and **dramatic storytelling.**
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a classical dance form that originated in the southern state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
 
• It is known for its** grace, symmetry, and expressive storytelling.**
 
 
 
• **Manipuri** is a classical dance form that originated in the northeastern state of **Manipur. **
 
 
• **​**It is known for its** fluid movements, delicate footwork, and devotional themes.**

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?

options.text: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Preamble **of the Constitution of India is an introductory statement that sets out the **objectives, principles, and purposes **of the Constitution.
 
• It was adopted on **26th November 1949 **by the **Constituent Assembly** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• The Preamble declares India to be a **sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic,** and **republic nation.**
 
• It also enshrines the ideals of** justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity,** which form the basis of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fraternity** means a sense of **brotherhood or unity **among people, and it assures human dignity by promoting the values of **mutual respect and compassion.**
 
• **Equality of status **and** opportunity **means that all individuals are **equal **before the law and have** equal opportunities to work **and earn a livelihood.
 
• **Justice, social, economic, and Political **means that the Constitution seeks to establish a just society that ensures **social, economic, and Political equality** for all citizens.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote 'Anand Math' from where India's National song 'Vande Mataram' has been taken?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee **was a prominent** Bengali writer and novelist** who is best known for his novel **'Anand Math'.**
 
• This novel is set in the backdrop of the** Sannyasi Rebellion** in the late 18th century and revolves around the theme of **patriotism and nationalism.**
 
• The novel 'Anand Math' is also known for its contribution to the** Indian independence movement.**
 
• The song **'Vande Mataram' **which is the national song of India, was first introduced in this novel.
 
• It became a popular patriotic song during the** freedom struggle** and played a significant role in unifying the people against the British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abanindranath Tagore** was a famous** Indian painter** and the **nephew** of Rabindranath Tagore. 
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** was a renowned **Indian poet, writer, and philosopher. **
 
 
• **​**He is best known for his work **'Gitanjali' **and was the first Indian to receive the **Nobel Prize for Literature.**
 
 
 
• **Mohammad Iqbal** was a famous** Urdu poet and philosopher** who is also known as **Allama Iqbal.**
 
 
• He is best known for his poem** 'Saare Jahaan Se Achha' **and is considered to be one of the most important figures in South Asian literature.

• The state of Himachal Pradesh is located in the **northern part of India** and is known for its scenic beauty, snow-capped mountains, and rich cultural heritage.
 
• Hinduism is the dominant religion in Himachal Pradesh, and there are several **ancient temples and shrines** dedicated to various Hindu deities in the state.

questions.question: The characteristic garlicky odour of garlic is due to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sulphur.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Garlic** belongs to the **Allium family **of vegetables, which also includes **onions, leeks, and shallots.**
 
• When garlic is **chopped or crushed,** it releases an enzyme called **alliinase**, which converts **alliin **(an amino acid) into **allicin **(an organosulfur compound).
 
• Allicin is responsible for the** pungent smell and taste** of garlic.
 
• When allicin breaks down, it produces a variety of **sulfur-containing compounds**, including** diallyl disulfide, allyl mercaptan, and allyl methyl sulfide**, which give garlic its characteristic garlicky odour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iodine** is a chemical element that is essential for the production of **thyroid hormones** in the body.

 
 
• It is often used as a **disinfectant **and in the treatment of **thyroid disorders.**
 
 
 
• **Copper** is a metal that is commonly used in **electrical wiring, plumbing, and construction**.
 
 
• It is also an important nutrient for the human body and is involved in the production of **red blood cells.**
 
 
 
• **Chlorine** is a chemical element that is commonly used as a **disinfectant in swimming pools **and **drinking water.**
 
 
• It is also used in the production of many** household and industrial chemicals.**
 
 
 
• **Sulphur **is a chemical element that is found in many** minerals and organic **compounds.
 
 
• It is used in the production of **fertilizers, pesticides,** and other chemicals.
 
• It is also an important nutrient for** plants and animals.**

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was established in 1885?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Congress.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian National Congress** was established in **1885** by **Allan Octavian Hume, Dadabhai Naoroji, Dinshaw Wacha,** and others.
 
• The Indian National Congress aimed to unite and** mobilize the Indian people **against British colonial rule and to promote** Indian interests and rights.**
 
• In addition to leading India's **independence from the UK,** the Congress had a big impact on other** anti-colonial nationalist movements** throughout the British Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Communist Party of India **was founded in **1925** and was influenced by** Marxist-Leninist ideology.**

 
 
• It played a significant role in the **Indian independence movement **and** subsequent politics.**
 
 
 
• **Muslim League** was established in **1906** to represent the interests of **Indian Muslims**, who feared marginalization in the predominantly Hindu Congress.
 
 
• The League later demanded a **separate Muslim state**, which led to the **partition of India in 1947.**
 
 
 
• The **East India Company **was a **British trading and colonial organization** that played a major role in India from the 1600s to the 1800s.
 
 
• However, the Company was **dissolved in 1858**, well before 1885.
